pep_line: Peptides are short chains of amino acids. Here every amino acid is a cell, so each peptide looks like itself.
pep_bpc157: A 15 amino acid piece of a protein found in stomach juice. Most of the research so far is in animals, on the gut lining, tendons and soft tissue.
pep_tb500: A short piece of thymosin beta 4, a protein the body uses to move cells into place and repair tissue. Research is mostly in animals, on recovery after injury.
pep_glp1: Copies of a gut hormone that tells the brain you are full and helps manage blood sugar. Semaglutide and tirzepatide are FDA approved for diabetes and weight.
pep_nad: Strictly a coenzyme, not a peptide: every cell uses it to turn food into energy and to repair DNA. Levels fall with age, which is why longevity research looks at it.
pep_sermorelin: A 29 amino acid copy of the start of the hormone that tells the pituitary to release growth hormone, so the body makes its own on its usual rhythm.
pep_note: A licensed physician decides what fits you, and some peptides cannot be prescribed at all. Nothing here is medical advice.

x_bpc157_benefits: Studied for tendons, ligaments and the gut lining.
x_bpc157_risks: Very little human research. Not FDA approved, and the FDA has raised safety questions about compounded versions. Banned in sport.
x_bpc157_dose: No established human dose: it has not been through human trials.
x_bpc157_stack: Stacking adds unknowns to unknowns. A physician adds one thing at a time.
x_tb500_benefits: Studied for recovery after injury and wound healing.
x_tb500_risks: Mostly animal evidence. Not FDA approved, and the FDA has raised safety questions about compounded versions. Banned for athletes.
x_tb500_dose: No established human dose, since there are no human trials to set one.
x_tb500_stack: Often paired with BPC-157 online, but the pair has never been studied in people.
x_glp1_benefits: FDA approved for diabetes and weight. Major weight loss in large trials; fewer heart attacks and strokes in heart disease.
x_glp1_risks: Nausea and stomach side effects are common. Rare: pancreatitis, gallbladder. Not with certain thyroid cancers in the family.
x_glp1_dose: Follows the FDA label: one shot a week, starting low and stepping up every few weeks.
x_glp1_stack: With insulin or other diabetes medicines, blood sugar can drop too low: a physician plans it.
x_nad_benefits: Studied for energy, healthy aging and metabolism.
x_nad_risks: Benefits in people are still unproven. Infusions can cause flushing, nausea and chest tightness.
x_nad_dose: Depends on the form: capsules of its building blocks, shots, or slow infusions. Slower means fewer side effects.
x_nad_stack: Little evidence for combinations: one change at a time shows what works.
x_sermorelin_benefits: Growth hormone and IGF-1 play roles in sleep, recovery and body composition.
x_sermorelin_risks: Injection site reactions, headache, flushing. A history of cancer needs a careful conversation first.
x_sermorelin_dose: Short-lived, so usually daily, often at night when growth hormone pulses. Adjusted by IGF-1 labs.
x_sermorelin_stack: Stacking with other growth hormone peptides raises the risks and needs close monitoring.
